text: When morning came. <break time="0.8s" /> The correspondent saw a tall wind tower. <break time="0.8s" /> On the shore. <break time="0.8s" /> Standing with its back. <break time="0.8s" /> To the tiny men like a giant. <break time="0.8s" /> Nature, he thought. <break time="0.8s" /> Was neither cruel nor kind. <break time="0.8s" /> Nor wise. <break time="0.8s" /> But simply indifferent. <break time="0.8s" /> To the struggles of men. <break time="0.8s" /> Fearing that they would soon be too weak. <break time="0.8s" /> The captain decided. <break time="0.8s" /> To take the boat through the surf. <break time="0.8s" /> At once. <break time="0.8s" /> A great wave crashed over them. <break time="0.8s" /> The boat turned over and the four men were thrown. <break time="0.8s" /> Into the icy water. <break time="0.8s" /> The oiler swam strongly ahead. <break time="0.8s" /> The cook floated on his back. <break time="0.8s" /> With an oar. <break time="0.8s" /> And the captain held on to the overturned boat. <break time="0.8s" /> The correspondent was caught. <break time="0.8s" /> In a current that held him back. <break time="0.8s" /> But at last a big wave. <break time="0.8s" /> Threw him safely toward the beach. <break time="0.8s" /> Then a man from the shore. <break time="0.8s" /> Ran into the water. <break time="0.8s" /> And pulled the cook to land. <break time="0.8s" /> And the captain sent him on to the correspondent. <break time="0.8s" /> On the sand lay the oiler. <break time="0.8s" /> His face turned down to the beach. <break time="0.8s" /> And he would never row again. <break time="0.8s" /> That night the white waves. <break time="0.8s" /> Moved in the moonlight. <break time="0.8s" /> And the wind carried the seas great voice. <break time="0.8s" /> To the three men on shore. <break time="0.8s" /> Who felt that they could now be its interpreters.
